chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
"Do not pray the Maghrib prayer until you join (with the 'Asr prayer), even if one-third of the night has passed."
ai.seo_question: When should the Maghrib prayer be performed during Hajj at Muzdalifah?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific timing for *Jam' al-Ta'khir* (delayed combination) of Maghrib and 'Asr at Muzdalifah, emphasizing that the pilgrim must wait for the arrival at the station rather than praying early. The mention of 'one-third of the night' highlights the flexibility of the timeframe, ensuring the prayer is performed within its proper time despite the delay caused by the journey from Mina. This ruling underscores the practical ease (*taysir*) granted to pilgrims during the critical transition between the two holy sites.
